change: useSupportedCountries now retries a failed GET /countries with bounded backoff (500/1500/3500 ms) before surfacing any error, and exposes retry() so the UI has an escape hatch after retries are exhausted. Pending timers are cleared on unmount so a queued retry cannot fire against a dead component.
why_smallest_safe: The defect is that ONE transient failure is terminal for the only entry point to the product. The minimal correct fix is to make transient failures non-terminal. Retries are BOUNDED (4 attempts total) so a genuinely down API is not hammered, the error path still reports the real API message, and no validation, security control or ordering guarantee was touched — the server remains the single source of truth for country grouping and order.

why_not_weakening: Nothing was granted. An authorization decision was neither moved nor relaxed — the client simply stops asking a question it already knows the answer to.

change: listPublicQuotes() now falls back to computing the sellable catalog on demand when the materialized pricing_quotes table is empty, instead of returning []. The membership rule (skip null-price corridors and lawyer_flag SKUs) was extracted into an exported isSellableCatalogEntry() type guard now used by BOTH the materializer and the fallback, so the two cannot price differently.
why_smallest_safe: pricing_quotes is derived data with a single writer. The page already had every input it needed; only the derived table was missing. The fallback reuses the exact same engine call the recompute job makes (quoteWith) and stays strictly read-only — it deliberately does NOT upsert or write an audit row, so a public unauthenticated GET can never write to pricing_quotes. The cache-hit path is untouched and still short-circuits before any recompute.
why_not_weakening: No internal economics are exposed: the fallback returns the same margin/cogs/band-stripped PublicQuote shape as the cached path, asserted by a dedicated test. The checkout gate is a separate authoritative recompute and is unchanged.

change: The scan now allowlists the local-demo TOKENS instead of exempting a file: stripLocalDemoJwts() parses each JWT payload it finds and neutralises only those whose claims carry iss === 'supabase-demo' (the keys `supabase start` prints on every machine). Everything else still trips the scan, in .gitleaks.toml or anywhere else.
why_smallest_safe: Adding '.gitleaks.toml' to the EXEMPT list was the one-line fix and was deliberately rejected — it would blind the scanner to a real secret pasted into that file. Allowlisting by issuer keeps the check sharp everywhere and needs no maintenance when the allowlist file changes.
why_not_weakening: Coverage went UP, not down: previously any content in an exempt file was unscanned; now only two specific published tokens are recognised as non-secrets, and they are verified by decoding the payload rather than by string match. A malformed payload is treated as a finding, not as safe.
